title: Toys R Us Set to Leave Japan After 35 Years
paragraphs: For many people, Toys R Us brings back memories of being a kid. Its big stores, filled with toys and games, could once be found around the world.
Japan is part of that history, with Toys R Us opening its first store there 35 years ago.
But now, Toys R Us Japan, which currently runs about 150 Toys R Us and Babies R Us stores in the country, is set to leave the Japanese market by the end of the year.

Pan Pacific International Holdings (PPIC), the company that owns discount store chain Don Quijote, will acquire the stores from Toys R Us Asia, the Hong Kong-based parent company of the Japanese business.
PPIC plans to rebrand the stores and develop a new business model.
The first Toys R Us store in Japan opened in 1991. And even when its former US parent company went bankrupt in 2017 and closed all 735 of its stores, the Japanese company continued doing business.
However, the company has been losing money for years. Japan's falling birthrate means there are fewer children, while the growth of online shopping has also hurt the business.

But while Toys R Us is leaving Japan, the brand is making a comeback in the US. It recently announced plans to open 120 new stores across the country with partner Go! Retail Group, bringing its US total to 160.
Toys R Us Asia will still have stores elsewhere in the region, including in China, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand.
And the brand can still be found in other parts of the world, including Canada, the UK and throughout Europe.
But in Japan, after more than three decades, the Toys R Us story will soon be coming to an end.
